tool.description: Create or update one entity and optional relationships. Use for KB mutations after validating intent; prefer a dryRun:true call first because it validates without writing and returns semantic advisor receipts for prose-heavy requirements. Use kb_model (mode requirement) before hand-writing strict property facts from prose, and kb_model (mode predicates) before hand-writing ontology predicate facts. Use the `relationships` array for batch creation of multiple links in a single call (e.g., linking a requirement to multiple tests or facts). An update keeps the properties and relationships it leaves out: send the fields that change (with title and status) and only the links to add. Prefer modeling requirements as reusable fact links (`constrains`, `requires_property`, or `requires_predicate`) so consistency and contradiction checks remain queryable. Relationship endpoints must already exist in KB. For requirements, the write will be rejected if it contradicts existing current requirements that constrain the same subject with incompatible properties. To replace a conflicting requirement, include a `supersedes` relationship from the new requirement to the old one in the same request, then upsert the old requirement with status closed (kb_check blocks a superseded requirement that is not closed). Successful writes may return non-blocking semantic advisor warnings; inspect and repair those warnings before treating prose as contradiction-checkable. Pass a sectioned `document.body` when creating a requirement (the statement, then `## Context` stating why it exists, who asked and the source, then `## Source` with the verbatim excerpt) and a prose body for scenarios, tests, ADRs and observation facts; a result warning reports an entity whose body lacks context, and kb_check blocks it under entity-context-missing. Never invent a reason the requester did not give: write 'Reason not stated'. Do not use for read-only inspection. Side effects: writes KB, may refresh symbol coordinates; dryRun:true writes nothing.

document.description: Optional source document write; omit body on update to keep it. New requirements take statement, Context, Source.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview without writing the KB or workspace; use it as the preflight before the real write.

id.description: Unique entity ID named by the behavior it governs (<TYPE>-<area>-<behavior>); an existing ID updates the entity.

implementedBy.description: req only: the declarations that implement it, each {sourceFile, symbol}; Kibi links each with implements.

plannedFacts.description: dryRun only: fact payloads (e.g. kb_model applyPlan entries) staged before this one, so their links resolve.

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).

properties.description: Entity fields; must include title and status. Fact, symbol, test and proof fields: kibi-usage resource operation-fields.

approval_ref.description: Requirement-only. Optional reference to the exception's approval decision record.

approved_by.description: Requirement-only: the human who approved this exception requirement.

firmness.description: req/adr only: firm (a human's rule, needs origin.ref), default or exploratory. Absent = default if an agent wrote it.

origin.description: Optional provenance: kind (human, agent, migration, import) and authority (ref, approved_by, recorded_at).

approved_by.description: The person who reviewed and approved this entity's content, not the approved_by of an exception requirement.

kind.description: Who authored the entity: human, agent, migration (backfilled by kibi migrate) or import.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 time the provenance was recorded.

ref.description: Source reference for the authored content: URL, document path, ticket, commit or conversation id.

rationale.description: Requirement-only: why it exists, in the stater's words; send it in the same write when they gave one, never invent one.

required_evidence.description: Requirement-only: weakest evidence level it accepts. Absent = tested if firm, else unverified.

semantic_text.description: Requirement-only authored prose used for semantic inventory hashes and UTF-8 spans.

sourceFile.description: Optional code source file for symbol entities. Example: 'src/auth/login.ts'.

status.description: Required lifecycle state; allowed values depend on the entity type. Examples: 'open', 'passing', 'accepted'.

symbol_role.description: Optional role classification for symbol entities. Example: 'behavioral'.

title.description: Required short title. Example: 'Protect account settings endpoint'.

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).
Entity type to create/update. Allowed: req, scenario, test, adr, flag, event, symbol, fact. Example: 'req'.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tool.name: kb_upsert
